subproblem.title: Area formula for the blow-ups of an injective regular image (step 3)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, g : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, B ⊆ ℝ^n a Borel set, z ∈ ℝ^n, s > 0 and f : ℝ^P → ℝ an arbitrary function. Assume g is differentiable at every a ∈ B, g is injective on B, and Dg(a) is injective for every a ∈ B. Notation:
- B_s := {b ∈ ℝ^n : z + sb ∈ B}.
- η_{w,s}(y) := s^{-1}(y − w) (SimonGMT blowUpMap).
- J(a) := √det(Dg(a)* ∘ Dg(a)), where Dg(a)* is the adjoint; this is Simon's Jacobian J_g, Ch. 2 (3.3).
Then ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(g(B))} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J(z + sb) · f(s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z))) dL^n(b). Here H^n = μHE[n] on ℝ^P and L^n is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n. Both sides are Bochner integrals, with value 0 for non-integrable integrands.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (g : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (z : Euclid n) (s : ℝ) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), MeasurableSet B → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ g a) → InjOn g B → (∀ a ∈ B, Injective (fderiv ℝ g a)) → 0 < s → ∫ y in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap (g z) s '' (g '' B), f y ∂μHE[n] = ∫ b in {b : Euclid n | z + s • b ∈ B}, Real.sqrt (((fderiv ℝ g (z + s • b)).adjoint ∘L fderiv ℝ g (z + s • b)).det) * f (s⁻¹ • (g (z + s • b) - g z))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Step 3 of the parent proof. It applies the area formula for injective maps with injective derivative to the rescaled map φ_s: Simon Ch. 2, §3, (3.2), with the weighted form (3.5). In SimonGMT this is the Bochner identity Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative, valid for every integrand. Here B is an arbitrary Borel set (the parent uses B = B_r(c)), and z need not lie in B.
Notation: w := g(z); φ(b) := s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − w); B_s := {b : z + sb ∈ B}.

1. (B_s is Borel.) The affine map b ↦ z + sb is continuous, hence Borel measurable. B_s is the preimage of the Borel set B under this map, so B_s is measurable.

2. (Derivative of φ.)
- Let b ∈ B_s and a := z + sb ∈ B, so g is differentiable at a.
- The map b' ↦ z + sb' has derivative s·id at b. By the chain rule, b' ↦ g(z + sb') has derivative Dg(a) ∘ (s·id) at b.
- Subtracting the constant w leaves the derivative unchanged; multiplying by the scalar s^{-1} multiplies it by s^{-1}. So φ is differentiable at b with Dφ(b) = s^{-1}·(Dg(a) ∘ (s·id)).
- For every v, s^{-1}·Dg(a)(sv) = s^{-1}s·Dg(a)v = Dg(a)v, by linearity and s ≠ 0.
- Hence Dφ(b) = Dg(z + sb). It is injective by hypothesis, since z + sb ∈ B.

3. (φ is injective on B_s.) Let b, b' ∈ B_s with φ(b) = φ(b'). Multiplying by s gives g(z + sb) − w = g(z + sb') − w, so g(z + sb) = g(z + sb'). Both z + sb and z + sb' lie in B, and g is injective on B, so z + sb = z + sb'. Hence sb = sb', and b = b' because s ≠ 0.

4. (φ(B_s) = η_{w,s}(g(B)).)
- If b ∈ B_s, then φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − w) = η_{w,s}(g(z + sb)) with z + sb ∈ B. So φ(b) ∈ η_{w,s}(g(B)).
- Conversely, let y = η_{w,s}(g(a)) with a ∈ B, and put b := s^{-1}(a − z). Then z + sb = z + (a − z) = a ∈ B, so b ∈ B_s, and φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(a) − w) = y.

5. (Area formula.) Let E = ℝ^n and F = ℝ^P. By steps 1–3:
- B_s is measurable;
- φ is differentiable at each point of B_s with injective derivative;
- φ is injective on B_s.
The Bochner area formula therefore gives, for the function f, ∫_{φ(B_s)} f dμHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫_{B_s} J_φ(b) f(φ(b)) dμHE[finrank ℝ E](b). No integrability is needed: both sides are Bochner integrals and the formula is an identity for every integrand. Here J_φ(b) := √det(Dφ(b)* ∘ Dφ(b)) is the metric Jacobian of φ. This is SimonGMT's areaJacobianAt φ b, which equals the square root by areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp.

6. (Normalisation.) finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n, so both measures are μHE[n]. On ℝ^n, μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure L^n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). By step 4, the left side is ∫_{η_{w,s}(g(B))} f dH^n.

7. (Jacobian.)
- For b ∈ B_s, step 2 gives Dφ(b) = Dg(z + sb). Hence J_φ(b) = √det(Dg(z + sb)* ∘ Dg(z + sb)) = J(z + sb), and φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z)).
- B_s is measurable, so the integrand on the right may be replaced on B_s (setIntegral_congr_fun).
- This gives ∫_{η_{g(z),s}(g(B))} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J(z + sb) f(s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z))) dL^n(b). ∎

Implementation note (not part of the mathematics). Add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea`; it is prebuilt and already imported by accepted DAG nodes.

- Prove `HasFDerivAt φ (fderiv ℝ g (z + s • b)) b` from (((hdiff _ hb).hasFDerivAt.comp b h1).sub_const (g z)).const_smul s⁻¹, where h1 := ((hasFDerivAt_id b).const_smul s).const_add z. Finish with HasFDerivAt.congr_fderiv and ContinuousLinearMap.ext, using map_smul, smul_smul and inv_mul_cancel₀.
- Rewrite the image, then finrank_euclideanSpace_fin and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume n.
- On B_s, rewrite Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp and the derivative identity before unfolding φ; then use smul_eq_mul.
proof_key_steps: B_s = {b : z + sb ∈ B} is Borel. φ(b) = s^{-1}(g(z + sb) − g(z)) is differentiable on B_s with Dφ(b) = Dg(z + sb), which is injective.
φ is injective on B_s (g is injective on B and s ≠ 0), and φ(B_s) = η_{g(z),s}(g(B)), using b = s^{-1}(a − z).
The Bochner area formula for φ on B_s gives ∫_{φ(B_s)} f dH^n = ∫_{B_s} J_φ · (f∘φ) dH^n.
Since finrank ℝ^n = n, H^n = L^n on ℝ^n, and J_φ(b) = √det(Dg(z+sb)*Dg(z+sb)) on B_s, the identity follows.
